geographic.groundContactBasis: Original standard Protomaps20261020/Mapzen201x201/6m grid retained from the Berlin pergamon_museum extract. Open front provider[0,8] supplies36.67228538201867m datum. Boundary grades-1.480..0.747m; working floor+.15m, closed foundation-1.660m. Only occupied museum footprint is ground-masked; outside forecourt/approaches and independent buildings/roads/water remain original. Exact threshold/accessibility remain approximate; no bespoke terrain, survey lookup or flattening. Outdoor colonnade posts follow the original terrain individually with bases0.15m below local ground. Its mapped U-shaped roof is triangulated through support centers at5.2m above original ground and edge controls, retaining actual ground/paths underneath. Skyline keeps the whole roof and selected end supports. This is an explicit coarse-DEM fit approximation to historic roof levels; no ground samples are edited. Qualified approximate native exterior fit accepted after inspecting the current complete site, east facade, covered roof courts/domes and exposed lower entrance/colonnade. Low-side plinth exposure and uphill burial remain. The west native view is partly occluded by the retained independent James-Simon-Galerie proxy; full source/shared renders cover the hidden facade. Exact threshold/accessibility and historic colonnade roof levels remain unverified.

buildingCutout.basis: Q157316 and OpenStreetMap way18578139/native35184390666971 identify Neues Museum. Reused the existing standard pergamon_museum Berlin extract; the parent and seven integral overlapping body/roof records are replaced. Detailed parts identify the central hall, both glazed court roofs, two corner domes and two wing relations; they are museum parts, not neighboring buildings. The exact 12-vertex outline supplies meter scale. Origin is the center of the mapped eastern central risalit front edge; internal X south-southeast along the long facade, Z east-northeast toward Kolonnadenhof. Native east/up/south geometry is baked, heading0. Adjacent James-Simon-Galerie, Pergamon and Alte Nationalgalerie building records remain independent. The shared exterior Kolonnadenhof colonnade way133885752/native35184505974584 is a ninth owned record: the complete U-shaped roof and open supports are modeled together, rather than deleting only its front segment. It is separate from all neighboring museum buildings and garden ground remains untouched.

groundCutout.basis: Occupied main museum footprint only; the shared outdoor colonnade retains original terrain and uses individually grounded supports.
